headline: South Asia: Pakistani national killed, 11 wounded as Riyadh airport hit by Houthi strike
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Pakistani national killed, 11 wounded as Riyadh airport hit by Houthi strike.
- Africa: Zaporizhzhia airstrikes kill 17 as Russia intensifies attacks across Ukraine.
- Persian Gulf Region: Iran urges Saudi Arabia to pursue diplomacy after Houthis escalate attacks.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Vector, Nammo expand push to mass-produce armed drones.
- Military Times, 2 hours ago: Vector, Nammo expand push to mass-produce armed drones.
Executives from both companies say they’re scaling up production of systems that reflect “the realities of how warfighters will employ them.”
The Caribbean - bottom line: Harris wants early guilty pleas to count in more cases.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: Harris wants early guilty pleas to count in more cases.
President of the Advocates’ Association of Jamaica (AAJ), Tamika Harris, is calling for greater recognition of early guilty pleas in Jamaica’s criminal justice system, arguing that they can spare victims further trauma and help reduce court backlogs. “Encouraging early guilty pleas is not about rewarding criminal conduct. It is about promoting accountability, protecting victims and ensuring the timely administration of justice.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: Appeal court slashes trespass award in Manchester land row.
THE COURT of Appeal has slashed a $400,000 damages award to $150,000 while upholding a finding of trespass against the Simmonds family in a long-standing Manchester land dispute between neighbouring families. The Morgan family – comprising Marylyn Morgan, her sister Melva Morgan, and her son Jason Salmon – took the Simmonds family to court in 2017, alleging trespass after members of the family began constructing a house on land in Swaby’s Hope, Spur Tree, Manchester, which the Morgans claimed to have possessed and used for over 40 years.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russian attack on Dnipro kills one person, sparks fire at shopping centre.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Russian attack on Dnipro kills one person, sparks fire at shopping centre.
A Russian attack on Dnipro killed one person on 12 October, while a separate strike on Dnipro district caused a fire at a shopping centre.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Russians strike business in Pavlohrad.
Regional officials have reported damage to a company in Pavlohrad following a Russian attack, though full details on casualties remain under assessment.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Zelenskyy: If Russia wants us to stop hitting refineries, it must stop strikes on our energy system.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that halting long-range strikes on Russian oil exports requires Russia to cease targeting Ukraine's energy system and civilian infrastructure.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Russians strike postal operator's logistics facilities in Odesa Oblast.
A Russian attack damaged a building's facade, windows and equipment in southern Odesa Oblast. No injuries have been reported.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Trump’s NATO envoy calls for moving military forces east as US reviews troops in Europe.
- Politico Europe, just now: Trump’s NATO envoy calls for moving military forces east as US reviews troops in Europe.
Matthew Whitaker called for an overhaul of NATO’s bases and military infrastructure to move forces eastward as America reviews its troop presence in Europe.
- Politico Europe, one hour ago: ‘This deal doesn’t help’: Europe slams Trump’s plan to buy Russian diesel.
"Pressure, pressure, pressure on Russia" is the only way to end the war, Lithuania's foreign minister said.
- Balkan Insight, 2 hours ago: Bosnia’s New Grand Mufti Looks Forward After Election by Muslim Community.
Nedzad Grabus vows progress after winning vote to become new supreme head or Grand Mufti of Bosnia's Islamic Community, a post he will hold for the next seven years.
- Politico Europe, 3 hours ago: Berechenbare Risiken – unberechenbare Politik? Warum Deutschland jetzt aus Worten Gesetze machen muss.
Mit berechenbaren Risiken kann die forschende Pharmaindustrie umgehen - mit politischer Unberechenbarkeit nicht. Warum eine Standortklausel nun ein erster Schritt in Richtung Verlässlichkeit am Standort Deutschland sein kann.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Zaporizhzhia airstrikes kill 17 as Russia intensifies attacks across Ukraine.
- Africanews, one day ago: Zaporizhzhia airstrikes kill 17 as Russia intensifies attacks across Ukraine.
Zaporizhzhia was hit by deadly Russian airstrikes on Saturday, 10 October, killing at least 17 people, including three children, Ukrainian officials said. Rescuers searched rubble for survivors as the city faced renewed strikes on residential areas.
- Africanews, 3 hours ago: Houthi rebels claim new strikes on Saudi airports and energy facilities.
Major airports in Saudi Arabia were hit by fresh attacks on Sunday, killing one person and injuring 11 others at King Khalid International Airport in the capital Riyadh.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 5 hours ago: Sudan: Air Strikes Kill Dozens of Gold Miners on Sudan-Egypt Border.
[DW] A Sudan-based rights group said 72 people were killed in a remote, disputed area known for illegal gold mining.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 7 hours ago: Sudan: Sudan Condemns Suicide Drone Attacks On El-Obeid.
[SNA] Khartoum (SUNA) - The Government of the Republic of Sudan strongly condemned the attacks carried out against the city of El-Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan State, on Friday using suicide drones, attributed to the rebel Rapid Support Forces (RSF) militia. According to preliminary information, the attacks resulted in civilian injuries and damage to homes and property.

- Al Jazeera - Middle East, The Hindu - International, one hour ago: Iran urges Saudi Arabia to pursue diplomacy after Houthis escalate attacks.
Tehran offers to facilitate talks between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis following deadly strikes on the kingdom.

US, Australia, Canada, Japan, South Korea and New Zealand among countries urging citizens to avoid travel to the kingdom.

Heavy clashes have been reported between Houthi fighters and Yemeni- forces near the strategic southern city of Taiz.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Pakistani national killed, 11 wounded as Riyadh airport hit by Houthi strike.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 7 hours ago: Pakistani national killed, 11 wounded as Riyadh airport hit by Houthi strike.
A fresh Houthi strike hit Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday, killing one person — a Pakistani resident — and wounding 11 others, a day after another deadly attack claimed by the Yemeni group forced authorities to suspend operations there. Saturday’s attack, the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade, was a sharp escalation in the Yemen war, where Riyadh has long militarily supported the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 16 hours ago: Emergency, governor's rule imposed in KP as president approves cabinet decision.
Key developments: Emergency imposed under Article 232, governor’s rule under Article 234 Cabinet recommended move due to KP govt’s ‘deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism’ Technocratic council formed; Fakhr Alam appointed as KP chief secretary PTI’s Gohar condemns decision as undemocratic, says peace cannot be established by weakening provincial autonomy Governor Kundi calls for unity for ‘new chapter’ in KP’s development ISLAMABAD: The federal government on Sunday imposed an emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa following the president’s approval of the recomme
- Dawn (Pakistan), 18 hours ago: Maaz Sadaqat, Imran Randhawa star as Pakistan thrash Sri Lanka in second T20I to seal series.
Maaz Sadaqat hit a blistering 96 before Imran Randhawa’s miserly spell helped Pakistan thrash Sri Lanka by 82 runs in the second Twenty20 International and seal the three-match series for the hosts here at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Sunday. Both Maaz and Imran were able to make a match-winning impact in what was only their second T20I outing after making their debuts in Friday’s opening match.
- Dawn (Pakistan), NDTV - Top Stories, Ukrainska Pravda, The Hindu - International, Al Jazeera - Middle East, one hour ago: Trump proclaims ‘energy ceasefire’ in Ukraine war.
KYIV: US President Donald Trump claimed on Sunday that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to what he described as an “energy ceasefire”, hours after Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky had pushed back against US pressure for a unilateral end to strikes on Russian refineries. In a social media post, Trump said the energy ceasefire would take effect immediately, but did not elaborate further. In an interview with Axios, Zelensky said Trump’s post was the first he had heard of the deal, though a senior Ukrainian official told Reuters that Ukraine was ready to agree to such a ceasefire, if Russia was.
Korean Peninsula - bottom line: North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles, fourth test in a month.
- NK News, Al Jazeera - Middle East, Yonhap News Agency, South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles, fourth test in a month.
North Korea fired multiple suspected ballistic missiles on Monday morning, according to Japanese and South Korean military authorities, the country’s fourth apparent missile test in the last month. South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) said North Korea fired “multiple ballistic missiles from the Pyongyang area toward the East Sea” at around 9:20 a.m. KST. […]

Asia - bottom line: How shadow banking feeds Myanmar while starving its military.
- South China Morning Post - China, 11 hours ago: How shadow banking feeds Myanmar while starving its military.
On a recent Friday night in a Bangkok dive bar, a group of young Myanmar exiles sang softly along to a mournful ballad played on an acoustic guitar. None among the crowd had any plans to leave, either for their homeland or home for bed. They fled war, a broken economy and forced conscription into a military that seized power in the 2021 coup. While their future in Thailand is uncertain, their ties to home are kept alive by the hard currency they send back each month to parents and siblings left...
- South China Morning Post - China, Al Jazeera - Middle East, one hour ago: Australian man rejects UAE links to Flydubai cockpit attack: ‘false accusations’.
A Melbourne man whose Islamic community centre has been linked by prosecutors in the United Arab Emirates to the co-pilot who allegedly attacked the captain of a Flydubai jet has hit out at “false accusations”. The Omani co-pilot, now in custody in the UAE, had drawn inspiration from al-Qaeda’s September 11, 2001 suicide attacks, and carried out his attempt “with the aim of causing the greatest possible loss of life”, according to the Emirati prosecutor’s findings published by state media last...
- South China Morning Post - China, just now: AI fuelling growth while putting Asia’s young workers at risk, IMF meeting hears.
An investment surge into artificial intelligence may be helping prop up a global economy battered by energy supply shocks, but the technology’s potential to cull jobs requires swift mitigation if Asia’s youth are to secure a place in the future workforce, delegates were warned at the IMF–World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Monday. Soaring energy prices, persistent inflation and mounting debt framed the opening of the week-long summit, which was last hosted in the Thai capital in...
- South China Morning Post - China, just now: Global diesel shortage: why Gulf refined fuel exports lag crude oil shipments.
Global diesel prices remain near record highs as Gulf producers struggle to restore refined-fuel exports, despite a recovery in crude shipments and pledges by more countries to release reserves. Net diesel exports from Gulf countries averaged 390,000 barrels per day in August, just over a quarter of their levels before the US-Israel war on Iran, according to the latest available data by the International Energy Agency (IEA) published in September. One obstacle to recovery is that Persian Gulf...
India - bottom line: Manipur on boil again: Naga body gives 48-hour ultimatum to return man’s severed head.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: Manipur on boil again: Naga body gives 48-hour ultimatum to return man’s severed head.
A civil society organization has given a 48-hour ultimatum for the return of a severed head. The headless body of Ajinbou R was brought for post-mortem following a militant attack in Manipur. Violence in the region has intensified with recent killings and ongoing tensions between Kuki and Naga tribes. The Chief Minister has condemned the violence and called for measures to ensure safety.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: 20k cops in schools, 80k edu institutions inspected as Poland tackles youth violence.
Poland is deploying 20,000 police officers to educational institutions after three stabbings occurred within four days. Prime Minister Donald Tusk emphasised the alarming rise in violence among young people. Authorities connected some violent behaviour to content glorifying violence on the internet and in video games. Reports highlighted recent attacks, including one involving a 15-year-old. The government is committed to ensuring the safety of children in schools.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar’s US Army job: Finding coders the Army doesn’t know it has.
Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar, a lieutenant colonel in the US Army Reserve, told CBS News his main job is helping the Army find soldiers who can code. Working with the Army’s personnel department, he says skilled programmers in junior ranks have no clear career path. Sankar joined Detachment 201, the Army’s Executive Innovation Corps, in 2025 alongside Meta’s Andrew Bosworth and OpenAI veterans Kevin Weil and Bob McGrew.
- NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: Sunil Bharti Mittal Conferred Highest Civilian Award Of France.
Mittal has been conferred the distinction in recognition of his longstanding commitment to deepening economic ties between India and France and his outstanding achievements in telecommunications and digital infrastructure, a company statement said.
